original_test_intent: Trigger the fatal SWD condition for each applicable DIMM and voltage comparator, prove the fault was on SWD/railtype3, observe the expected reset, and verify that rail D, DIMM training and memory service fully recover.
original_method: Use the PMIC datasheet to bind SWD, railtype3 and voltage types to registers/status; map every DIMM and PMIC I2C address; create explicit tuples; baseline SWD voltage/status and SPD; inject one comparator under OOB capture; correlate fresh SWD fatal evidence; validate boot, training and memory; restore PMIC/I2C ownership and telemetry before another run.
manual_activity: The PMIC owner identifies the SWD register and physical rail, authorizes each comparator/PMIC tuple, monitors the fatal run and restores rail, bus and memory state.
required_inputs: PMIC register/datasheet proof railtype3 selects SWD and definitions of voltagetype0/1
Complete DIMM socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm and PMIC part/address mapping
BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/OOB path and expected SWD register response
Vendor-correct command continuation and explicit per-target tuple list
SWD nominal voltage, tolerance, current/thermal envelope and abort thresholds
Fresh SWD PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL fields, reset/boot/training timeouts, memory-health criteria and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated instrumented SUT with independent recovery console and SWD telemetry
Confirm physical PMIC/rail target and preserve status/SPD/memory baseline
One comparator on one DIMM per run with mandatory restoration and health gate
Abort on wrong rail bit, unsafe electrical reading, boot/training failure, DIMM disappearance, I2C loss or evidence ambiguity
No automated target iteration; restore PMIC recovery/mode, SPD control, telemetry, I2C and HDT
agent_execution_scope: Validate SWD register mapping, comparator, target/I2C topology, electrical envelope and evidence plan
Collect read-only rail/status telemetry, settings, OOB/CPER/BERT/SEL, DIMM training and memory health
Do not infer rail/target, change PMIC/I2C/BIOS/HDT, inject, reset, repeat, recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve SWD rail and target matrix
Approve electrical/fatal evidence and recovery gates
Restore state and issue per-tuple verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic PMIC/power logs cannot prove the SWD status register, voltage comparator or physical DIMM selected by railtype3.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Execute one mapped railtype3 comparator only after SWD register approval, correlate SWD status and persistent reset evidence, then verify rail and memory recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: listvalidumc, 0:0:3, railtype3, voltagetype0/1, dimm0, immediate reset, all-DIMM scope, PMIC/I2C settings and 360/120-minute values remain preserved but gated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run SWD as a serialized physical-rail matrix with register-specific proof and full DDR5 recovery between targets.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds SWD status decoding, physical/I2C mapping, explicit tuples, electrical aborts, source-specific durable fields and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A fixed dimm0 command and generic fatal reset cannot prove every SWD target or comparator.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect rail selection or incomplete restoration may leave a DIMM unstable or make later PMIC cases unsafe.

project_override_considerations: Treat all PMIC I2C access as BMC/platform-management scope under the Wistron rule. Maintain SWD evidence separate from SWA/SWB/SWC and VIN rails, even when the host reset pattern is identical.
expected_evidence: SWD/railtype3/voltagetype register map and full DIMM/PMIC/I2C topology
Pinned tool/spec with raw SWD voltage/status, SPD and BIOS baseline
One exact command and OOB reset/boot timeline per tuple
Fresh SWD-specific PMIC status plus CPER/BERT/SEL source/severity
Restored electrical readings, complete training/enumeration and clean bounded memory exercise

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Every DIMM and both voltage types are requested, yet only fixed 0:0:3/dimm0/voltagetype0 is supplied. Command continuation and tuple expansion are undefined. Railtype3-to-SWD, comparator meanings and rail-specific electrical acceptance are unproven.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The SWD fatal purpose and seed tuple are identifiable. Vendor rail mapping and safety limits can be provided without changing the preserved source.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 91 Wistron-System RAS-00811-V002: provide PMIC register proof railtype3=SWD and voltagetype0/1 semantics; map every DIMM to socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm, PMIC part/address and Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/OOB path; approve command continuation and full tuple matrix; define SWD electrical limits/status, PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL evidence, reset/boot/training deadlines, memory recovery, aborts and restoration.

review_improvement: Requires SWD-specific register and electrical proof and turns the all-DIMM instruction into an auditable physical target matrix with restoration gates.
independent_technical_reasoning: SWD coverage cannot be inferred because adjacent rail types are separate tests that may produce the same reset. The meaningful discriminator is the PMIC SWD status/telemetry at the mapped address. Each voltage comparator and DIMM can have different electrical behavior, so one fixed tuple is insufficient; memory training and a clean workload after rail restoration are necessary before another fatal injection.
